head: 4b382e5388e652308d2beca448666630ba6c332d
summary: Failed check lookups now retain HTTP status internally and avoid misleading JSON errors. The command output still omits that status, leaving the intended user outcome incomplete.
reasons: The change correctly distinguishes a failed lookup from malformed JSON, but the intended diagnostic benefit stops short of the command output.
The two-file change matches the planned scope, reuses Error.from_gh, and adds no dependencies or configuration. The packet reports passing validation and one review round without substantive repairs.
Incident frequency and live rate-limit behavior remain unknown; neither establishes a need for a broader error-handling redesign.
concerns: skills/shaka/lib/shaka/github/check_list.rb preserves HTTP 403 only in Error#http_status, while skills/shaka/scripts/shaka.rb:358 prints only e.message. Agents and maintainers running shaka pr still receive a generic exit-1 error without the promised HTTP status or rate-limit diagnosis.
alternative: Keep the narrow fix and expose the extracted HTTP status in the check-lookup error message, including the required-check wrapper. This preserves stderr privacy and existing failure safeguards without adding a new reporting system.
next_action: Revise this PR to include the extracted HTTP status in the displayed check-lookup error, and verify that output through the command boundary.
